answer.location_description: Top-right corner of the crop, roughly rows 1-6 and columns 17-23, at the image border away from the central nodule.
answer.shortcut_type: bright patch/marker in the top-right corner (non-nodule image region)
answer.mechanism: Several 'periphery' layer-1 units carry unusually dense, strong positive weights in the top-right corner while weighting the centre negatively. These are units 19, 25, 2, 16, 14, 18 and 20. The most concentrated ones are 19, 25, 2, 16 and 14. Their linearised layer-2 to output pathway is negative: about -10.8k for unit 19, -20k for unit 25, -11.5k for unit 2, -5k for unit 16 and -10k for unit 14, in integer-product units. So brightness in that corner pushes the logit toward benign. Units 18 and 20 route positively, which partly offsets this.
answer.evidence: First-layer weights start uniform within about ±80 integer units (1/sqrt(576)/scale), so values beyond ±80 must have been learned. Counting such values for the periphery units in 7x7 corner boxes gives about 33 in the top-right box. The other corners give about 22 (top-left), 19 (bottom-right) and 17 (bottom-left). Examples in the top-right: unit 19 has r3c18 87, r3c22 88, r4c19 92, r4c21 85, r4c22 91, r5c20 87 and r6c20 88. Unit 18 has col19 r2-r4 at 82, 92, 93 and r5c22 85. Unit 25 has r4c19 86, r4c21 85 and r4c22 82. Unit 2 has col22 r2, r3 and r6 at 89, 86 and 92. Unit 16 has r1c22 89, r5c20 87 and r5c22 85. Unit 20 has r1c23 90 and r5c20 89. Caveats: the asymmetry is only about 3 SD, these units also weight the periphery positively in general, and second-layer weights stay within initialisation range. The evidence is therefore moderate rather than conclusive.
answer.main_feature: Units 3, 8, 21, 24, 27 and 28 have strong positive weights over the central region (rows ~4-20, peak values 94-99), so they respond to central nodule density and size. Unit 3's pathway, for example, pushes toward malignant. Centre-negative/periphery-positive units (2, 14, 18, 19, 25, 29, 30) contrast the nodule with its surroundings.
